---
description: 'Report design, naming, UX consistency, and accessibility standards'
applyTo: '**'
---

## Report Design Standards

Use Title Case business names for reports.

Use clear business labels for page names.

Do not use generic names such as Page 1 or Sheet2.

Use Dev as a development artifact suffix when needed by deployment policy.

Rename all visuals and bookmarks in the Selection pane before report submission.

Name visuals with visPurposeName.

Name bookmarks with bmPurposeName.

Keep slicer placement, filter pane behavior, and drill-through patterns consistent across pages.

Use bookmarks for controlled interactivity such as toggling detail panels and switching views.

Meet WCAG 2.0 AA contrast requirements for text and meaningful visual elements.

Provide alt text for all informative visuals.

Describe what the visual communicates in alt text, not only the chart type.

Do not use color as the only encoding for critical meaning.

Supplement color with labels, patterns, or icons.

Ensure all report pages are keyboard navigable.

Set tab order in the Selection pane to match logical reading flow.

Use these naming examples:

| Good | Avoid |
|---|---|
| visSalesTrendByMonth | Chart |
| visTopCustomersTable | Table 1 |
| bmOpenDetailsPanel | Bookmark1 |
| Executive Summary | Page 1 |
